# Evaluating ∫ 2x³eˣ dx

I'll use the **tabular method** for repeated integration by parts.

## Setup

| Differentiate (u) | Sign | Integrate (dv) |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 2x³ | + | eˣ |
| 6x² | − | eˣ |
| 12x | + | eˣ |
| 12 | − | eˣ |
| 0 | + | eˣ |

## Multiplying along diagonals with alternating signs

$$+ (2x^3)(e^x) - (6x^2)(e^x) + (12x)(e^x) - (12)(e^x) + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
$$\frac{d}{dx}[2x^3 e^x - 6x^2 e^x + 12x e^x - 12e^x]$$
$$= (6x^2 e^x + 2x^3 e^x) + (-12x e^x - 6x^2 e^x) + (12e^x + 12x e^x) - 12e^x$$
$$= 2x^3 e^x \checkmark$$

## Final Answer

<answer>2*x**3*exp(x) - 6*x**2*exp(x) + 12*x*exp(x) - 12*exp(x) + C</answer>
